No copyright renewal found in U.S. Copyright Office, 2012."; Notes "Photograph by Pacific & Atlantic Photos, Inc. Forms part of: New York World-Telegram and the Sun Newspaper Photograph Collection".

Photograph by Pacific & Atlantic Photos, Inc.; New York World-Telegram and the Sun Newspaper Photograph Collection, Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, LC-USZ62-123429. items.reason: Licence confirmed on the LoC record. The first record said "unknown photographer"; LoC credits the agency Pacific & Atlantic Photos, Inc. (defunct; LoC searched and found no renewal) - attribution corrected. Authentic 1929 gelatin silver press print, sharp, good tonal range. Scan carries a black film-holder border, a white print margin, a torn top-left corner and a pencilled number in the left margin: must be cropped. Identifiable faces are of people photographed in public in 1929; no personality concern.
items.whatItShows: Elevated view of the corner of Broad and Wall Streets: a dense crowd of men in fedoras and overcoats fills the lower half, three 1920s cars and a mounted policeman are stranded in it, and the pale stone New York Stock Exchange (fluted columns at upper left) and the arched doorway of the adjoining building rise behind. A "CAUTION speed limit 8 miles per hour" sign stands at right.
items.subjectRegion: Crowd fills the bottom 50% edge to edge, densest and largest bottom-centre and bottom-right; the cars sit left of centre at 45-70% height; the caution sign at 85% x, 55-70% y.
items.negativeSpace: No dark quiet area. The upper half is pale, fairly even stone wall (light grey, low detail) especially upper right between the windows and the arch: text there needs dark type or a scrim. The NYSE column bays upper-left are mid-dark stripes.
items.depthStructure: Three clear layers: foreground hats and shoulders (large, bottom third), middle ground of cars, horse and thinner crowd on the street, and the flat building facade as a backdrop wall. Ground plane rises steadily with height in frame, so depth separation is good and smooth; the facade is a near-planar far layer.
items.tonalNotes: Full range (p1 3, median 117, p99 242). Blacks are in the hats, coats and car bodies in the lower half; highlights are the stone facade and hat brims. Top half light, bottom half dark: a natural light-to-dark vertical split.
items.cropAdvice: Crop to the image area: roughly x 3.5%-95.5%, y 6.5%-93.5% of the scan removes the black border, white margin and pencil number; to lose the torn top-left corner as well start the crop at about y 14% (or crop left edge in to x 35% for a tighter frame).

items.licenseEvidence: Commons API extmetadata: LicenseShortName "Public domain", Artist "Unknown author", Credit = link to beeldbank.spaarnestadphoto.com (a commercial picture library), Date 1929. Wikitext carries only {{PD-anon-70-EU}} {{PD-US}} with an empty Permission field. No deletion or dispute notice. There is no statement from Spaarnestad Photo / Nationaal Archief that the image is free, and neither the anonymity of the author nor publication in 1929 is documented anywhere I could read.
items.attribution: Crowd in front of the New York Stock Exchange during the crash, 1929. Photographer unknown, collection Spaarnestad Photo SFA001006911, via Wikimedia Commons.
items.reason: Rejected on licence, not on the picture. The public-domain claim rests entirely on a Commons uploader assertion for an anonymous press/agency photo whose source is a commercial image bank that sells licences; the two facts the PD tags depend on (anonymous author, published in 1929) are not evidenced. Real-world risk is low (a 1929 press photo published in 1929 is out of US copyright and past the 70-year anonymous-work term), so the owner could choose to reinstate it, but I cannot confirm it. Also the smallest file in the set (1920x1510; the 2865x2253 original was not downloaded). The LoC NYSE crowd image covers the same subject with a confirmed licence. Authentic photograph, no watermark or border.
items.whatItShows: Street-canyon view down Broad Street from beside Federal Hall: hundreds of people and a jam of 1920s cars and trucks recede into the distance, two mounted policemen in the foreground, the colonnaded NYSE at right, Wall Street Journal and Western Union signs on distant buildings.
items.subjectRegion: Crowd and vehicles fill the lower 55%, converging to a vanishing point at about 25% x, 40% y; mounted police at centre-bottom (40-60% x, 75-95% y).
items.negativeSpace: Solid near-black column fills the left 17% of the frame from top to 60% height; dark car roofs along the bottom edge. NYSE facade upper right is mid-grey striped.
items.depthStructure: Strong one-point perspective: foreground cars and horses, mid-ground crowd, far street and building wall, with a near dark column at left as a framing plane. Excellent depth separation.
items.tonalNotes: Contrasty and dark (median 63, p1 3, p99 255); deep blacks in column, cars, horses; highlights on pavement and facade.

Rights Advisory: "No copyright restriction known. Staff photographer reproduction rights transferred to Library of Congress through Instrument of Gift." Notes: "NYWT&S staff photo." The LoC collection rights page (076_nyw.html, capture 2019-12-31) states: "NYWT&S staff photographs are in the public domain per the instrument of gift."
items.attribution: Depositors gather in the rain outside the failed Bank of United States, New York, 1931. World-Telegram staff photograph; Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division, NYWT&S Collection, LC-USZ62-117261.
items.reason: Licence confirmed: staff photograph, dedicated to the public by the instrument of gift. Authentic press print. Kept but not hero-grade in my view: foreground figures are motion-blurred, the scan is of a copy negative with moderate sharpness, and the print carries four heavy black grease-pencil editor crop marks inside the image area (top centre, right edge, bottom centre, lower centre) that cannot be removed by cropping without losing about a third of the frame. Black scan border and white margin must be cropped. Protest placards are legible ("We demand prosecution of all directors", "U.S. government liable...") - historical, no concern.
items.whatItShows: High-angle view of a rain-soaked New York square: a crowd of several hundred depositors under dark umbrellas, with dozens of white protest placards scattered through the middle of the crowd; wet reflective paving, park trees, lamp posts and subway kiosks behind.
items.subjectRegion: Crowd fills the lower 70% of the image area; the white placards cluster in a horizontal band at 35-60% height across the centre; large umbrellas and standing figures bottom right.
items.negativeSpace: Little true quiet space. The top band (upper 20%) is soft grey tree foliage at left and pale wet pavement at right; bottom-left corner is pale empty pavement. Bottom-right is dark massed coats. Text would need a scrim.
items.depthStructure: Continuous receding ground plane seen from above: large foreground figures and umbrellas at the bottom, placard band in the middle, emptier wet plaza and park at the top. Depth is gradual rather than layered; umbrellas give many small bumps, which should make a lively point cloud.
items.tonalNotes: Full range (p1 1, median 131, p99 251). Blacks: umbrellas and coats, scattered as dots. Highlights: white placards, straw hats and wet pavement. Overall mid-grey, busy, speckled texture.
items.cropAdvice: Crop off scan border and margin: about x 4.5%-96%, y 4%-95.5%. To avoid the grease-pencil marks take x 5%-85%, y 22%-72% (still about 3270x1650 px) or expect to retouch the four marks.

items.reason: Kept on the strength of NARA's own "Unrestricted" use statement, which I read on the catalogue record. Caveat: the Commons PD-USGov reasoning is wrong - this is not a federal employee's work but a press print from the New York Times Paris Bureau file that the government later acquired; the photographer/agency is unidentified. NARA nonetheless publishes it as unrestricted and it is very widely reproduced. Source page corrected to the NARA record; the download URL in the first record was also stale (current Commons original is under /f/f8/). Authentic, sharp press print with good contrast, no watermark, no border. Bank signage is a defunct brand; no trademark concern.
items.whatItShows: Corner view from above of the American Union Bank at W 37th St: a crowd of depositors, many in straw boaters, pressed around the closed corner entrance beneath a large dark sign "SAFE DEPOSIT VAULTS / AMERICAN UNION BANK / 4% paid on thrift accounts"; arched bank window at right, a delivery truck in the bottom-right corner, a street full of cars and a bus receding up the left side.
items.subjectRegion: Crowd occupies 5-70% x, 40-90% y, densest centre-left; the big sign sits at 36-52% x, 10-35% y; arched window 57-90% x, 8-55% y; truck bottom right (72-100% x, 62-100% y).
items.negativeSpace: Upper right corner and the strip above the arch are plain pale wall (light, quiet). The sign panel and the bank windows are large dark rectangles but already carry lettering. Bottom-left pavement/kerb is mid-grey and fairly quiet.
items.depthStructure: Foreground: truck and handcart bottom right, pedestrians bottom left. Middle: crowd against the building corner, which is a strong vertical edge at 45% x. Background: street receding diagonally to the upper left with cars, bus and hazy buildings. Good separation between the building planes and the receding street.
items.tonalNotes: p1 37, median 93, p99 247: darkish with slightly lifted blacks (no pure black; a levels tweak will help). Darks in sign, windows, suits and truck; highlights in the stone wall, straw hats and white shirts.
items.cropAdvice: No border to remove. A square crop on x 0-78% keeps crowd, sign and street; a wide crop y 5-75% drops the foreground truck.

items.reason: NARA states unrestricted use on the item record. Same caveat as the other 306-NT item: the print came from a newspaper bureau file, creator unidentified, so the public-domain basis is NARA's determination rather than federal authorship. Authentic, sharp, rich blacks; the best single image in the cluster. Thin white print margin along the bottom and right edges and a clipped left edge of the banner ("[SO]UP") - crop slightly. Faces are identifiable individuals photographed in public in 1931; no concern. The Al Capone attribution is NARA's caption.
items.whatItShows: A long queue of unemployed men in overcoats, flat caps and fedoras along a wet pavement, running from a storefront doorway at left away to the right edge, beneath a large white banner reading "FREE SOUP COFFEE & DOUGHNUTS FOR THE UNEMPLOYED"; dark brick wall with "Parking 25c" and "Horan Bailiff" signs behind at right. Several men look at the camera.
items.subjectRegion: The queue forms a horizontal band at 45-78% height spanning the full width, figures largest at left and shrinking to the right; the white banner is top-left (0-62% x, 0-27% y).
items.negativeSpace: Bottom 22% is empty wet pavement, mid-grey and quiet: the best place for text. The dark shop window (33-60% x, 25-50% y) and the dark doorway (13-32% x, 30-70% y) are near-black panels; the upper-right brick wall (65-100% x, 0-30% y) is dark and quiet apart from the Horan sign.
items.depthStructure: Foreground: empty pavement and the three men standing apart at far left. Middle: the line of men receding diagonally left to right. Background: shopfront plane at left stepping back to the brick wall and fence at right. Clear separation of figures from the dark wall, strong diagonal recession.
items.tonalNotes: p1 21, median 120, p99 231: balanced, good blacks in coats, window and brick; highlights in the banner, light overcoats and hats, and the sheen on the pavement.
items.cropAdvice: Trim about 1% off the right and 1.5% off the bottom to remove the white print margin. A 2:1 wide crop on y 22-80% keeps the queue and the lower banner line.

items.licenseEvidence: Commons API extmetadata: LicenseShortName "Public domain", Artist "Berenice Abbott", Credit = NYPL item link, template PD-USGov-WPA, no deletion notice. NYPL Digital Collections item 510d47df-3362-a3d9-e040-e00a18064a99 (live page is script-rendered, read via Internet Archive capture 2018-01-12): "The New York Public Library believes that this item is in the public domain under the laws of the United States, but did not make a determination as to its copyright status under the copyright laws of other countries." Suggested credit: "From The New York Public Library".
items.attribution: Berenice Abbott, Broad Street looking toward Wall Street, Manhattan, 16 July 1936. "Changing New York", Federal Art Project (WPA). From The New York Public Library, Photography Collection. Public domain in the United States.
items.reason: Public domain in the US as a work made for the federal WPA Art Project, confirmed by NYPL's rights statement. Flag: NYPL expressly makes no determination outside the US, and Abbott died in 1991, so in countries that apply life+70 without regard to US government origin the status is formally unsettled; these WPA Abbott images are used freely worldwide and I accept it under the US-federal-work rule, but the owner should know. "Schwartz's Restaurant" sign is a defunct business; no trademark concern. Authentic large-format photograph, extremely sharp, full tonal range, no border or watermark. Note the date (1936) is seven years after the crash; caption accordingly.
items.whatItShows: Portrait-format view up the Broad Street canyon: a black vertical "SCHWARTZ'S RESTAURANT" sign in the left foreground, tall office facades stepping back along the left, the pyramid-roofed Bankers Trust tower at top centre, the NYSE columns in sharp perspective on the right, Federal Hall's portico small at the end of the street, and a handful of 1930s cars on the sunlit roadway.
items.subjectRegion: Vanishing point at about 72% x, 80% y (Federal Hall). The pyramid tower is at 43-60% x, 5-40% y. The restaurant sign occupies 0-17% x, 18-72% y. Cars at 30-80% x, 86-93% y.
items.negativeSpace: Bright empty sky in a tapering wedge at top centre-right (35-75% x, 0-25% y) - white, suits dark text. Dark quiet zones: the bottom-left corner (shadowed pavement and railings) and the left edge strip around the sign. The roadway at the bottom centre is smooth mid-grey.
items.depthStructure: Textbook one-point perspective with many layers: near sign and railings (left), near NYSE wall (right edge), successive building faces stepping back on the left, towers in the far centre, sky behind. Very strong depth separation; ideal for a depth point cloud.
items.tonalNotes: p1 19, median 118, p99 236. Blacks in the sign, the left-hand shadowed facades and the lower left; highlights in the sky, the sunlit right-hand stone and patches of road. Sides darker, centre lighter.
items.cropAdvice: No border. Portrait 4:5; for a landscape slot crop y 55-100% (street level with cars and Federal Hall) or y 0-45% (towers and sky).

items.reason: CC BY 2.0 confirmed and bot-reviewed; the newspaper itself was published in 1929 and its US copyright has expired. Attribution with licence link is mandatory. Genuine historical artefact, legible at full size. As an image it is a flat grey document (median 205, no blacks below about 58) with no depth - use only as a flat plane/texture or crop to the headline; it will not make a meaningful depth point cloud. Note the date: Monday 28 October 1929 (Black Monday), evening edition. The page also carries an unrelated lurid court story (Pantages trial) with a halftone portrait of a 17-year-old witness - crop to the banner headline to keep that out.
items.whatItShows: Flat scan of a complete broadsheet front page of the Santa Ana Register, Monday 28 October 1929, with the full-width banner "BILLIONS LOST AS STOCKS CRASH", a second deck about the Pantages trial, eight columns of small type, a halftone portrait at upper right-centre, and the right-hand column headed "MAINSTAYS OF MARKET IN PLUNGE".
items.subjectRegion: Masthead across the top 0-9% y; the crash banner headline spans the full width at 13-18% y; the crash story is the far-right column (84-100% x, 20-62% y). Halftone portrait at 58-80% x, 27-52% y.
items.negativeSpace: None in the usual sense: uniformly dense grey text on pale newsprint. No dark areas.
items.depthStructure: None - a single flat plane. Any depth would be synthetic.
items.tonalNotes: p1 58, median 205, p99 229: light and low-contrast, greyish paper with dark-grey ink. Needs a strong levels stretch (or inversion to white-on-black) to sit in a black-and-white layout.
items.cropAdvice: For impact crop to the masthead and banner: x 0-100%, y 0-19% (3840x965 px), or just the headline y 12.5-18.5%. Crash column alone: x 84-100%, y 19-62%.

items.reason: Rights statement read on the holding library's own record; a January 1929 Minneapolis Tribune press photo donated by the paper, so US copyright has expired. NoC-US speaks only to US status. Authentic press print with heavy genuine wear: torn top edge with two missing pieces (black scan background shows through), creases, a torn lower-left corner, and visible hand retouching on faces and outlines. Usable as a characterful secondary image, not a hero; fairly dark and soft. Caveats for captions: it is Minneapolis, not New York, and it shows a newly installed board nine months before the crash, with men posing - not clerks marking prices during the crash. Two of the men face the camera and are identifiable; 1929, no concern.
items.whatItShows: Two young board clerks in pale jackets stand on a low platform in front of a huge black quotation board headed "MINNEAPOLIS-S[T. PAUL] STOCK EXCHANGE", with columns of white stock names (Gen Mills, Munsingwear, NW Airways...) and empty ruled grids; seven men in dark suits stand on the floor in front, in two groups left and right, mostly seen from behind or in profile.
items.subjectRegion: Board fills the upper 65% edge to edge. Clerk one at 26-36% x, 22-67% y; clerk two at 66-77% x, 18-67% y. Suited groups at 2-30% x and 73-98% x, 28-88% y.
items.negativeSpace: Large dark, quiet board area in the centre between the two clerks (38-65% x, 10-63% y) and upper left: good for light text. The floor along the bottom 20% is pale and empty.
items.depthStructure: Shallow, stage-like: dark-suited men in the foreground, a pale step/platform edge, the two clerks one step back, and the flat board immediately behind them. Only about two metres of real depth; expect a weak, mostly planar depth map with figures popping slightly forward.
items.tonalNotes: p1 21, median 70, p99 205: dark overall, no clean whites. Blacks in the board and suits; lightest tones are the clerks' jackets, the platform riser and the floor.
items.cropAdvice: To lose the torn top edge and lower-left corner crop to about x 3-97%, y 12-92%. The damage can also be kept deliberately as an artefact edge.

items.reason: Licence confirmed on the LoC record; a 1922 copyright deposit is long expired in the US. Photographer unnamed. Authentic gelatin silver print, very sharp, scanned from the original. White print margin, a clipped top-left corner and a few dust specks and a small tear at top centre: crop the margin. Blacks are slightly lifted (p1 49) and the right-hand window wall is blown out, so apply a levels adjustment. Dates from 1922, seven years before the crash; no people.
items.whatItShows: Interior of the NYSE ticker control gallery, no people: a long dark wooden bench runs in perspective from the lower left to the right-centre distance, carrying two glass-domed stock tickers in the foreground, candlestick telephones, a plug switchboard, relay boxes and more domed tickers further back; bentwood chairs line a bright window wall on the right; veined marble wall panels fill the background, a relay panel stands at the far end.
items.subjectRegion: Bench runs diagonally from 0-45% x at 65-100% y up to 75% x at 47% y. The two glass-domed tickers are at 10-33% x, 60-80% y. Chairs along the right edge, 78-100% x, 50-100% y.
items.negativeSpace: Upper two-thirds of the left and centre is quiet mid-grey marble wall (20-70% x, 0-45% y) - good for text of either polarity with a slight scrim. Upper right (72-90% x, 0-30% y) and the floor at right are blown-out white. The bench top in the lower left is dark and fairly plain.
items.depthStructure: Strong diagonal recession along the bench: glass domes near, telephones and boxes mid, relay panel and table far; marble wall as a back plane; chairs form a second receding row on the right. Very good depth separation, though glass domes and the blown window may confuse a depth estimator.
items.tonalNotes: p1 49, median 123, p99 248: blacks are grey-ish until levels are set. Dark: bench, instruments, far-left wall panel. Bright: window wall, floor at right, papers on the bench. Left half darker, right half light.
items.cropAdvice: Crop off the white print margin: about x 1-99%, y 1.5-98%, which also removes the clipped top-left corner if started at x 3%, y 3%.
